Make Law 9 physics: a component is RED unless something measured says otherwise. Today Law 9 is prose in CLAUDE.md, which is policy — the thing Law 4 says is a tracked debt, not a resting state.

RULED SAME DAY (2026-08-04-the-spec-lives-in-akiens-head), and it changes what this ticket is building. Red is NOT a quality verdict — it is TRANSLATION DISTANCE. Akien: 'the picture in my head is the source of truth. it hasn't changed much in the last month. everything we talk about and make into tickets is trying to translate a pretty fixed spec in my head into english and thence to code. this source of truth in my head is why everything which is not that is red.' And the metaphor that makes it derivable: 'if this were a building site, anything slated for excavation would be red until its excavation was complete and had passed inspection. the whole building site starts red and slowly becomes green.' So the artifact this wants is closer to a SITE PLAN than to a health check — it must be able to show the lots nobody has broken ground on yet, which no test-result-derived signal can see. A component with no proofs, no code and no charter is the reddest thing on the site and is currently invisible to every scan we own.

Three states, derived proportionally to the component's nature. GREEN: a certificate was issued with findings green at that point in time; the certificate is the unforgeable proof. RED: the component's own code or controlling data changed since its last certificate, or it has never been proved — must re-run and earn a new certificate through the gate. YELLOW: something the component depends on changed, but the component itself did not — it keeps operating; where logs exist and show correct function, it presents operational evidence at the gate and earns a new certificate without human intervention (self-cleaning). Simple components (basic sieves) that keep producing correct output do not need re-review when neighbors change. Components without logging stay at their last certificate until a problem is observed — human observation closes the loop, and the penalty for being wrong about a simple thing is small (CP5, CP6). There is no perfect safety; the system learns from the gaps.
